semantic_candidates.evidence: A radius-12 sphere is retained for latitude -pi/4 through pi/3 and longitude span 3*pi/2, then closed by two horizontal and two meridian planes.

validation_findings.evidence: Both latitude bounds are strictly between the poles and the longitude span is positive, so all four circular arcs and five closure lines have positive length.
Two latitude circles, two meridian great circles, and five exact lines account for every unique edge.
The retained longitude interval is 3*pi/2 rather than a full U period, so its meridian boundaries are distinct.
STEPCAFControl_Reader with explicit empty processing flags imports the spherical segment, and BRepCheck rejects the resulting representation without repair.
The latitude interval [-pi/4, pi/3] lies strictly inside [-pi/2, pi/2], excluding both spherical poles.
The no-processing STEP round trip records 1e-7 millimetres, equal to 1e-10 metres, for every vertex, edge, and face tolerance.
The spherical patch, two latitude caps, and two meridian closures pair all nine unique boundary edges.
Every edge has exactly two incident face uses in one connected, pole-free closed component.
The processing-disabled XDE readback preserves the analytic entities but BRepCheck reports the imported representation invalid.

oracle.statement: The partial longitude and pole-free latitude ranges define one regular spherical patch. Two latitude arcs, two meridian great-circle arcs, four cap-to-meridian lines, and one shared axis line give nine edges and six vertices. Two horizontal caps and two meridian closures complete five faces, with every edge used twice.
